title: Negotiation Strategies
completion_message: ¡Excelente! En los negocios, no obtienes lo que mereces, obtienes lo que negocias. Conocer términos como 'Leverage' y 'Play hardball' te permite navegar cualquier negociación con autoridad.

parts.visual:
Tarde o temprano tendrás que negociar contratos o salarios. Conoce estos términos: 

1. Leverage (Ventaja / Apalancamiento): 
- El poder que tienes para influir en una negociación. 
Ej: Since we are their biggest client, we have a lot of LEVERAGE. 

2. Play hardball (Ser duro / Jugar rudo): 
- Actuar agresivamente en una negociación sin ceder. 
Ej: The union is PLAYING HARDBALL, refusing to accept any pay cuts. 

3. Compromise (Ceder / Llegar a un acuerdo medio): 
- OJO: En inglés, 'compromise' NO es 'compromiso' (commitment). Significa ceder o llegar a un acuerdo donde ambas partes renuncian a algo. 
Ej: We couldn't agree on the price, so we had to COMPROMISE.
parts.audio: Welcome to Negotiation Strategies. Sooner or later, you will have to negotiate contracts, deals, or salaries. Knowing the right terms is power. Number 1: Leverage. This is the power or advantage you have to influence a negotiation. For example: Since we are their biggest client, we have a lot of LEVERAGE. Number 2: Play hardball. To act aggressively or ruthlessly in a negotiation, refusing to yield. For example: The union is PLAYING HARDBALL, refusing to accept any pay cuts. Number 3: Compromise. Be careful here. In English, compromise does NOT mean commitment. It means to reach an agreement where both sides make concessions. For example: We couldn't agree on the price, so we had to COMPROMISE.

parts.visual:
4. Meet halfway (Llegar a un punto medio): 
- Una frase común para 'compromise'. 
Ej: You want $100, I want $50. Let's MEET HALFWAY at $75. 

5. Stalemate / Deadlock (Punto muerto / Estancamiento): 
- Cuando la negociación se traba y nadie avanza. 
Ej: The peace talks have reached a STALEMATE. 

6. Dealbreaker (Factor decisivo para romper el trato): 
- Una condición inaceptable que arruina toda la negociación. 
Ej: Not having health insurance is a DEALBREAKER for me. 

7. Bargaining chip (Moneda de cambio): 
- Algo de valor que usas para negociar. 
Ej: They used the new patent as a BARGAINING CHIP.
parts.audio: Number 4: Meet halfway. A very common phrase that means to compromise. For example: You want $100, I want $50. Let's MEET HALFWAY at $75. Number 5: Stalemate or Deadlock. A situation in a negotiation where no progress can be made. For example: The peace talks have reached a STALEMATE. Number 6: Dealbreaker. A condition or issue that is absolutely unacceptable and causes the negotiation to fail. For example: Not having health insurance is a DEALBREAKER for me. Number 7: Bargaining chip. Something of value that you use to gain an advantage in a negotiation. For example: They used the new patent as a BARGAINING CHIP.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige el término de negociación correcto.

questions.question: Because we hold the patent for the technology, we have all the ____ in this negotiation. (Ventaja/Poder).
The investors are playing ____. They won't give us the money unless we fire the CEO. (Jugando duro).
questions.explanation: Play hardball = actuar rudo, ser inflexible en una negociación.

questions.question: I wanted 10 days of vacation, they offered 5. We had to ____ and settle on 7 days. (Ceder/Punto medio).
questions.explanation: Compromise = ceder para llegar a un acuerdo (OJO: no es 'comprometerse a hacer algo').

questions.question: If you are willing to lower the price, we are willing to buy more units. Let's meet ____. (Punto medio).
questions.explanation: Meet halfway = llegar a un punto intermedio, ceder mutuamente.

questions.question: The negotiations have reached a ____. Neither side is willing to make a concession. (Punto muerto).
questions.explanation: Stalemate (o Deadlock) = punto muerto o estancamiento.

questions.question: I like the job offer, but the fact that I have to work on weekends is an absolute ____ for me. (Factor para cancelar el trato).
questions.explanation: Dealbreaker = condición inaceptable que rompe el trato.

questions.question: The union is holding a strike to use it as a ____ chip during the salary negotiations. (Moneda de cambio).
questions.explanation: Bargaining chip = moneda de cambio (algo que usas para negociar).

questions.question: To get what you want, sometimes you have to make a ____. (Concesión).
questions.explanation: Make a concession = hacer una concesión (ceder en algo).

questions.question: I'm not going to accept their first offer. I want to make a ____-offer. (Contraoferta).
It's a ____-____ situation. Both the buyer and the seller benefit from the deal. (Ganar-ganar).
questions.explanation: Win-win situation = situación donde todos ganan.

questions.question: A situation where one person wins only if the other person loses is called a ____-sum game. (Suma cero).
questions.explanation: Zero-sum game = juego de suma cero (lo que uno gana, el otro lo pierde).

questions.question: Before entering the room, know your BATNA: Best ____ to a Negotiated Agreement. (Alternativa).
questions.explanation: BATNA (Best Alternative to a Negotiated Agreement) = tu plan B si la negociación falla.

questions.question: They tried to ____ the price down by pretending they had another supplier lined up. (Presionar para bajar).
questions.explanation: Drive down the price = presionar/forzar el precio a la baja.

questions.question: We need to find some common ____ before we can move forward with the contract. (Puntos en común).
questions.explanation: Find common ground = encontrar puntos en común.

questions.question: He gave me a 'take it or ____ it' offer. There was no room for negotiation. (Lo tomas o lo dejas).
questions.explanation: Take it or leave it = lo tomas o lo dejas (oferta no negociable).

questions.question: The negotiations broke ____ after three days of arguing. (Fracasaron/Se rompieron).
questions.explanation: Break down = fracasar o romperse (las negociaciones).

questions.question: After weeks of deadlock, we finally had a ____. We found a solution! (Avance / Gran descubrimiento).
questions.explanation: Breakthrough = un avance o descubrimiento repentino que soluciona un problema.

questions.question: If they don't meet our minimum requirements, we are prepared to ____ away from the deal. (Alejarse/Abandonar).
questions.explanation: Walk away = abandonar la negociación sin acuerdo.

questions.question: Don't show your hand too early; keep your cards close to your ____. (Sé discreto con tu estrategia).
questions.explanation: Keep your cards close to your chest = no revelar tus intenciones o ventajas.

questions.question: We managed to ____ a deal just before the deadline. (Cerrar/Asegurar un trato golpeando/forjando).
questions.explanation: Strike a deal = cerrar o forjar un acuerdo (viene de 'strike a bargain').

stages.title: Written Expression
stages.description: Escribe el término de negociación correcto.

questions.question: We have the ____. (Poder de negociación / ventaja con L)
They are playing ____. (Jugando duro con H)
We had to ____. (Ceder/Llegar a acuerdo con C)
Let's meet ____. (Punto medio con H)
A complete ____. (Punto muerto con S)
That is a ____. (Factor que rompe el trato con D)
A ____ chip. (Moneda de cambio con B)
A ____-offer. (Contraoferta con C)
A ____-win situation. (Ganar-ganar con W)
____ a deal. (Forjar/Cerrar un trato con S)
